items.title: Bumper 🤖
items.text:
Bumper is a self-hosted replacement for Ecovacs cloud services. It lets supported Ecovacs robots and apps talk to a server on your local network, instead of the Ecovacs cloud.

Bumper emulates the web, MQTT, and XMPP services that the official app and robots use. Protocol fidelity matters: the app and robots are unmodified clients, so Bumper aims to match the behavior they expect.

Disclaimer

This project is a work in progress. Behavior varies by robot model, firmware, app version, and region. Check the documentation, Model Compatibility, and logs when troubleshooting.

items.title: 🧩 How it fits together
items.text:
For Bumper to work, app/robot traffic for Ecovacs domains must reach Bumper, and the client must trust the TLS certificate Bumper presents.

Official app / robot
        |
        | DNS resolves Ecovacs domains to your Bumper server
        v
   Bumper (web + MQTT + XMPP)

Bumper's web UI shows server status, connected sessions, registered bots/clients, and clean logs.

items.title: 🚀 Getting started
items.text:
Start with the step-by-step guide:

  • Getting Started Overview - the full setup path, in order.

In short:

  1. Configure DNS so Ecovacs domains resolve to Bumper.
  2. Create or provide certificates on the host if you use the checked-in Compose files.
  3. Deploy Bumper (Docker/Compose is recommended, usually behind nginx or Traefik).
  4. Connect the official app and make it trust Bumper's CA.
  5. Use robot Wi-Fi setup only when you need the app's onboarding flow.

items.title: 👀 What to expect
items.text:
• ecovacs.net shows only helperbot: normal when no robot or app client is connected. Robots appear after they connect to Bumper's services with working DNS, reachability/proxy routing, and certificate trust. See Getting Started troubleshooting and What to expect.
  • Model support is empirical: check Model Compatibility. Some models need certificate/key changes or have known limitations.
  • Cloud-only features may be missing: Bumper focuses on local control and the APIs needed for that.

If you are stuck, use Discussions and debug logs (DEBUG_BUMPER_LEVEL=DEBUG).

items.title: Bumper Origins & Maintenance
items.text:
The Bumper project was originally created by @torbjornaxelsson in 2017 as a reverse engineering tool to interface with certain EcoVacs robotic vacuums. It successfully reached its initial goal and remained in a stable (but no longer actively maintained) state, with the last update committed in December 2017.

In early 2019, @bmartin5692 picked up the project to support newer vacuum models that use updated protocols. His fork introduced key changes and improvements to the original codebase and continued development for several years.

Later, @edenhaus forked the project to refactor and modernize large portions of the codebase, aiming to clean up architectural issues, enhance maintainability, and support more recent devices. This fork has since diverged significantly and is now actively maintained as the primary development source going forward.

items.title: 🔧 Current Maintenance
items.text:
This repository is now the actively maintained version of Bumper. It includes:

  • Major refactors for stability and code clarity
  • Updated support for newer EcoVacs models and protocols
  • Improved documentation
  • Better compatibility with modern environments

items.title: 📦 Legacy Versions
items.text:
If you are looking for the older versions:

  • The original 2017 codebase by @torbjornaxelsson is archived.
  • The intermediate development fork by @bmartin5692 is still available.
  • A historical snapshot of the pre-refactor code is preserved as v0.1.0 in his fork.

Warning

That legacy version may still work with some early models (e.g. M81 Pro, N79S), but for all current and future use, this repository is recommended.

items.title: Environment Variables Overview
items.text: Bumper's behavior can be tailored by setting environment variables before startup. Below is a list of all variables that the Python application reads, grouped by category. Variables not listed here are hardcoded or not configurable via environment.

items.title: ⏰ Timezone
items.text: Variable Default Description TZ UTC Timezone for scheduling and log timestamps. Set to any IANA zone, e.g., Europe/Berlin. SYNC_TIMEZONE false Sync the server clock and timezone offset to robots when they connect over MQTT.

items.title: ⚙️ Feature Flags
items.text: Variable Default Description CA_CERT_API_ONLY_BUMPER_CERT false If true, only the self-signed Bumper CA is served. If false, the bundle also carries the original system CA. USER_USERNAME_DEFAULT bumper Username the local account is presented with. USER_NICKNAME_DEFAULT USER_USERNAME_DEFAULT Display name of the local account. Shown as the member name in the app. USER_MAIL_DEFAULT ${USER_USERNAME_DEFAULT}@home.local Mail address the local account is presented with. PHOTO_MAX_PER_DEVICE 20 How many uploaded files are kept per robot, pictures and cleaned maps alike. The oldest are dropped on every new upload. CLEAN_LOG_MAX_PER_DEVICE 100 How many clean log entries are kept per robot. The oldest are dropped on every new one. WEBVIEW_TRUSTED_HOST_SUFFIXES ecovacs.com,ecovacs.cn,ecouser.net,... Hosts the app may open in a webview. The app ships the Ecovacs domains as a fallback, add the host this instance is reached under.

items.title: 📁 Paths & Files
items.text: Variable Default Description BUMPER_DATA $PWD/data Directory for persistent data, uploads and caches. DB_FILE ${BUMPER_DATA}/bumper.db TinyDB database file. The file holds JSON, not SQL. BUMPER_ACCOUNT_KEY ${BUMPER_DATA}/account.key RSA key used to decrypt account fields the app encrypts. Mode 0600. BUMPER_CERTS $PWD/certs Directory for TLS certificate files. BUMPER_VOICES ${BUMPER_DATA}/voices Directory for the voice files the robot downloads. BUMPER_CODEPUSH ${BUMPER_DATA}/codepush Directory for the CodePush packages the app downloads. BUMPER_CA_CERT ${BUMPER_CERTS}/ca.crt Path to the CA certificate. BUMPER_CA is accepted as a deprecated alias. BUMPER_CA_KEY ${BUMPER_CERTS}/ca.key Path to the CA private key. BUMPER_CA_PEM ${BUMPER_CERTS}/ca.pem Path to the combined server key, server certificate and CA certificate. BUMPER_CERT ${BUMPER_CERTS}/bumper.crt Path to the server certificate. BUMPER_KEY ${BUMPER_CERTS}/bumper.key Path to the server private key.

items.title: 🔐 Certificates
items.text: Variable Default Description BUMPER_CA_VALID_DAYS 6669 CA certificate validity in days (about 18 years). Long duration for home-hosted self-signed stability. BUMPER_VALID_DAYS 666 Server certificate validity in days (about 22 months). Practical rotation cycle for home management. CERT_KEY_TYPE ec Key algorithm. Accepts only ec (P-256 elliptic curve) or rsa. CERT_RSA_KEY_SIZE 2048 RSA key size in bits. Must be 2048 to 4096. Ignored for EC keys.

items.title: 🔒 Authentication
items.text:
Variable Default Description TOKEN_VALIDITY_SECONDS 2592000 Portal-token session lifetime in seconds (30 days). ACCESS_TOKEN_VALIDITY_SECONDS 1800 OAuth access JWT lifetime in seconds (30 minutes). REFRESH_TOKEN_VALIDITY_SECONDS 2592000 OAuth refresh JWT lifetime in seconds (30 days). TOKEN_JWT_ALG Follows key type Algorithm used to sign app tokens. Defaults to ES256 for EC keys and RS256 for RSA keys.

Bumper does not verify Ecovacs request signatures. See Authentication for the full flow.

items.title: 🌐 Networking
items.text: Variable Default Description BUMPER_LISTEN Auto-detected via system DNS IP address or hostname to bind all server listeners (Web, MQTT, XMPP). BUMPER_ANNOUNCE_IP ${BUMPER_LISTEN} IP advertised to robots. If 0.0.0.0, set explicitly. WEB_SERVER_HTTPS_PORT 443 Port for the HTTPS web UI and API. WEB_SERVER_LISTEN_PORT 8007 Port for the plain HTTP web UI and API. MQTT_LISTEN_PORT 1883 Plain MQTT listener. MQTT_LISTEN_PORT_TLS 8883 TLS MQTT listener. XMPP_LISTEN_PORT_TLS 5223 TLS XMPP listener. HELPER_BOT_TIMEOUT 10 Seconds the helper bot waits for a robot to answer. The app gives up on a request after 15 seconds, so a longer wait is never seen by it. CODEPUSH_LOCAL_PACKAGE false Serve the CodePush package from this server instead of the cloud. The app then downloads it from the host of the CodePush service, which has to be one that the DNS override points at Bumper.

items.title: 🚦 Logging & Debugging
items.text: Variable Default Description DEBUG_BUMPER_LEVEL INFO Log level (NOTSET, DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR, CRITICAL). DEBUG_BUMPER_VERBOSE 1 Verbose output per log line (integer 0, 1, 2). DEBUG_LOGGING_API_REQUEST false Log incoming API requests. DEBUG_LOGGING_API_REQUEST_MISSING false Log requests that no route matches. DEBUG_LOGGING_XMPP_REQUEST false Log XMPP requests before internal changes. DEBUG_LOGGING_XMPP_REQUEST_REFACTOR false Log XMPP requests after internal changes. DEBUG_LOGGING_XMPP_RESPONSE false Log XMPP server responses. DEBUG_LOGGING_SA_RESULT false Log service-autonomy outputs from API requests by /sa.

items.title: 🔗 Proxy & Forwarding
items.text: Variable Default Description BUMPER_PROXY_MQTT false Forward MQTT traffic to the Ecovacs cloud. BUMPER_PROXY_WEB false Forward web traffic to the Ecovacs cloud. PROXY_PUBLISH_TIMEOUT 10 Seconds a proxied MQTT publish may wait before it is reported as timed out.

items.title: 🚢 Docker Compose & Swarm Variables
items.text:
These additional environment variables are used in the compose files to control service deployment and container behavior.

Variable Default Description ENV_FILE .env File the containers read their environment from. NODE_ROLE manager Docker Swarm role constraint for service placement (manager or worker). NETWORK_MODE bridge Docker network driver (bridge or overlay). RESOURCES_LIMITS_CPUS 1 CPU limit per container. RESOURCES_LIMITS_MEMORY 500m Memory limit per container. RESOURCES_RESERVATIONS_CPUS 0.001 CPU reservation per container. RESOURCES_RESERVATIONS_MEMORY 32m Memory reservation per container. VERSION_BUMPER latest Bumper image tag to deploy. The image reports its build version under the same name. VERSION_NGNIX 1.29-alpine3.22-slim NGINX image tag for the reverse proxy. TZ Europe/Berlin Timezone inside containers (binds to host timezone). BUMPER_ANNOUNCE_IP required IP advertised to robots. The shipped Compose files refuse to start when it is unset; outside them it falls back to BUMPER_LISTEN. BUMPER_LISTEN 0.0.0.0 Bind interface inside the container for Bumper listeners. DEBUG_BUMPER_LEVEL INFO Logging level inside containers. DEBUG_BUMPER_VERBOSE 1 Verbose detail per log line inside containers. PROTOCOL https Scheme the nginx health check uses against healthcheck.ecouser.net. LB_SWARM true Serve the Traefik routers through the Swarm load balancer. TRAEFIK_ENTRYPOINT https Traefik entrypoint the Bumper routers attach to.

The optional stacks keep their own variables in their Compose file: docker-compose-zensical.yaml uses VERSION_ZENSICAL, ZENSICAL_PORT, ZENSICAL_MAIN_PATH, MIKE_PORT, MIKE_BRANCH, MIKE_RELEASE_TAG and DOCS_UID/DOCS_GID, and docker-compose-mitm.yaml uses VERSION_MITMPROXY, MITM_PATH and MITM_WEB_PW.

items.title: Development Guide
items.text: This guide covers setting up a local development environment, running the application, and maintaining code quality.

items.title: 🔧 Prerequisites
items.text:
• uv (the repository commits uv.lock)
  • Python 3.15 recommended (3.13 and 3.14 are supported)
  • Git

uv can install the interpreter itself, so a system Python 3.15 is optional.

items.title: 🛠️ Setup Local Environment
items.text:
Step 1 - Clone the repository

git clone https://github.com/MVladislav/bumper.git
cd bumper

Step 2 - Create the virtual environment

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install uv

Installing uv inside .venv keeps it out of your system Python.

Step 3 - Install every dependency group

uv sync --active --all-groups

--all-groups includes the development and docs tools. Activate .venv once per shell; the rest of this guide uses uv run --active.

items.title: 🚀 Running the Application (local development)
items.text:
For normal deployments, use Docker behind a reverse proxy (nginx or Traefik). Running Bumper directly without the expected network/proxy setup is useful for development and debugging, but it is not the supported user deployment path.

bash scripts/certs/create-cert.sh
WEB_SERVER_HTTPS_PORT=8443 uv run --active bumper

The web UI is served at https://<BUMPER_LISTEN>:8443. BUMPER_LISTEN defaults to the address the hostname resolves to; set it explicitly (for example BUMPER_LISTEN=127.0.0.1) if the default is not the address you want.

Use uv run --active bumper --help to list CLI options. In containerized deployments, prefer Environment Variables.

items.title: 📚 Documentation
items.text:
Docs are Zensical pages. Two previews, pick one:

Preview Serves Version selector Live docs/ from disk no Versioned local gh-pages (latest + tags) yes

The live preview is for checking an edit. The versioned preview is for the selector and for a tag's own content; it is not needed to change code.

items.title: Host
items.text:
uv run --active zensical serve --dev-addr 0.0.0.0:8000

Open http://<host>:8000/bumper/.

Versioned, from the same checkout:

uv run --active mike deploy --ignore-remote-status latest
uv run --active mike set-default --ignore-remote-status latest
uv run --active mike serve --ignore-remote-status --dev-addr 0.0.0.0:8001

Open http://<host>:8001/. mike only redirects the site root, so a deep link must name the version (/latest/getting_started/dns/). Add a tag from a worktree, so the tag's own docs/ and mkdocs.yml are used:

MAIN="$PWD"
git worktree add --detach /tmp/bumper-release v0.4.1
cd /tmp/bumper-release
cp "$MAIN/mkdocs.release.yml" .
uv run --project "$MAIN" --frozen --no-sync mike deploy \
  --ignore-remote-status --config-file mkdocs.release.yml v0.4.1
cd "$MAIN"
git worktree remove --force /tmp/bumper-release

mkdocs.release.yml adds the mike version provider to a tag that predates it. Without it that tag has no version selector, so v0.4.1 has no way back to latest.

items.title: Docker
items.text:
Both are standalone. The zensical service only serves docs/; the mike service serves the versioned site.

docker compose -f docker-compose-zensical.yaml up -d zensical   # :8000
docker compose -f docker-compose-zensical.yaml up -d mike       # :8001
MIKE_RELEASE_TAG=v0.4.1 docker compose -f docker-compose-zensical.yaml up -d mike

Swarm uses the same file through the docker-swarm-compose alias:

docker-swarm-compose -f docker-compose-zensical.yaml bumper-docs
MIKE_RELEASE_TAG=v0.4.1 docker-swarm-compose -f docker-compose-zensical.yaml bumper-docs
docker stack rm bumper-docs

The mike service mounts ${ZENSICAL_MAIN_PATH:-$PWD} read-only and builds in /tmp/work inside the container, so the host checkout and its gh-pages branch are never modified. It rebuilds latest from the current docs, keeps watching the source and redeploys latest when docs change, reuses the other versions already on gh-pages, and adds the newest v* tag (or MIKE_RELEASE_TAG) so the selector can switch between them. The toolchain is cached in the docs_venv volume.

Remove a version with uv run --active mike delete --ignore-remote-status <version>.

GitHub Pages source

CI publishes to gh-pages. In Settings → Pages, use Deploy from a branch, branch gh-pages, folder / (root).

items.title: Linting & Static Analysis
items.text:
Run prek hooks

uv run --active prek run --all-files

The no-commit-to-branch hook rejects commits on main. Run the hooks from a feature branch, or skip that one hook when checking the rest:

SKIP=no-commit-to-branch uv run --active prek run --all-files

Type checking with mypy

uv run --active --frozen mypy bumper/

Linting with pylint

uv run --active --frozen pylint bumper/

items.title: Unit Tests
items.text:
Run tests

uv run --active pytest tests

Tests with coverage report

uv run --active pytest --cov=./ tests --cov-report xml --junitxml=pytest-report.xml

Generate HTML coverage report

uv run --active pytest --cov=./ tests --cov-report html:tests/report

The HTML report is located at tests/report/index.html.

For route registration, response envelopes, and choosing a template for a new endpoint, see Web API Endpoints.

items.title: 🔄 Updating Static Ecovacs Data
items.text: Bumper ships with pre-fetched Ecovacs data under bumper/web/static_api/. See Static Data Update Guide.

items.title: 🤝 Contributing Changes
items.text:
1. Fork the repo and create a feature branch.
  2. Follow the setup and testing steps above.
  3. Commit changes with clear messages and update tests.
  4. Open a pull request against main, ensuring all checks pass.

See the repository README and this development guide for contribution expectations. Pull requests should target main, follow Conventional Commits, and pass lint/type/test checks before review.

items.title: 📦 Static Data Update Guide
items.text:
Bumper serves some data from pre-fetched files under bumper/web/static_api/ instead of querying the Ecovacs cloud, so the app keeps working fully offline. This data changes over time; this guide explains which files exist and how to refresh them with the helper scripts in scripts/.

For user-facing behavior (voice languages, work logs/maps), see Features.

Note

The process is not fully automatable. update-eco-data.sh and some other scripts require an Ecovacs account login, and the first login from a new device may require an email verification code. The scripts are meant to be run manually by a maintainer.

items.title: 📦 What Gets Updated
items.text:
All files live in bumper/web/static_api/ and are served to the app from Bumper's own web server instead of the Ecovacs cloud:

File Served to the app at What it contains configGroupsResponse.json POST /api/pim/product/getConfigGroups Product groups with their robot models and Wi-Fi setup steps (product configuration screens) configNetAllResponse.json POST /api/pim/product/getConfignetAll All robot models with their Wi-Fi setup steps (steps, customSteps) productIotMap.json POST /api/pim/product/getProductIotMap classid → product info (QR-code decoding, bot list enrichment) updateCheck.json GET /v0.1/public/codepush/update_check deployment_key → latest bundle info (download_url, is_available, is_mandatory, …) updateCheck_mapping.json (lookup for the codepush update check) main_folder → deployment_key, resolves update checks sent by package name timezones.json GET /api/basis/time/timezones The time zones of the app, with their name in every language voices.json GET /api/pim/voice/get The voice of every language the app offers, with the file the robot has to download

items.title: 🔄 Scripts
items.text:
Script Needs login Reads Writes update-eco-data.sh ✅ (password + optional email code) Ecovacs private API configGroupsResponse.json, configNetAllResponse.json, productIotMap.json 1-update-eco-codepush.sh ❌ codePushConfig.json updateCheck.json 2-update-eco-codepush-mapping.sh ❌ updateCheck.json updateCheck_mapping.json 3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh ❌ updateCheck.json the CodePush packages in the CodePush directory update-eco-timezones.sh ✅ (password + optional email code) Ecovacs api base timezones.json update-eco-voices.sh ✅ (password + optional email code) Ecovacs portal API voices.json and the voice files in the voice directory

Most of the scripts are maintenance: they refresh the information Bumper serves, and the result is pushed into the repository. Run them when that information has to be brought up to date.

Two of them fetch files that are large and that stay out of the repository - the voice files and the CodePush packages. They are only needed when those files are to be served from Bumper instead of from the cloud.

The three CodePush scripts carry a prefix that matches their order inside the group. Run the scripts in this order when you refresh everything. Inside the CodePush group each script needs the output of the previous one; the other scripts are independent.

  1. scripts/data/update-eco-data.sh - logs in to the Ecovacs private API and downloads the per-country product configs (DE, US, other countries from COUNTRIES), combines them with the committed files and rewrites the download URLs to local domains (see combination rules).
  2. scripts/data/1-update-eco-codepush.sh - queries the public codepush update_check endpoint for every deployment key in codePushConfig.json and combines the results into updateCheck.json. Download URLs are stripped of their AWS signing parameters. Downloads run in parallel (ECO_PARALLEL).
  3. scripts/data/2-update-eco-codepush-mapping.sh - downloads the codepush bundles referenced by updateCheck.json, extracts the main folder of each bundle and writes the {main_folder: deployment_key} mapping used by the app (see payloads.py codepush_update_check).
  4. scripts/data/3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh - downloads the CodePush packages of the deployments, so that the app can update without reaching the cloud. Only needed when the packages are to be served from Bumper (CODEPUSH_LOCAL_PACKAGE). The packages are a few MB to a few dozen MB each and are not part of the repository: they land in the CodePush directory (BUMPER_CODEPUSH, ${BUMPER_DATA}/codepush by default). The script needs no login, but it needs the urls of updateCheck.json, so it runs after 1-update-eco-codepush.sh. Downloads run in parallel (ECO_PARALLEL).
  5. scripts/data/update-eco-timezones.sh - fetches the time zones the app shows, with their name in every language, and writes them to timezones.json.
  6. scripts/data/update-eco-voices.sh - fetches voice metadata (voices.json) and voice files. Voice files are not stored in the repository; they are written to BUMPER_VOICES (${BUMPER_DATA}/voices by default). See Features for user-facing behavior and requirements.

All scripts write their per-run artefacts to json_mappings/ (gitignored) and copy the final files into bumper/web/static_api/. All outputs are sorted, so re-runs produce stable diffs.

Note

Run the scripts before the DNS override is in place, or from a machine that can still reach the Ecovacs cloud. The DNS override points cloud names at Bumper.

Note

Voice files and CodePush packages are exceptions to "everything ends up in static_api/". They are large and fetched from the cloud, so they are kept out of the repository on purpose.

items.title: 🚀 Usage
items.text:
Step 1 - Refresh the product data (needs an Ecovacs account):

ECOVACS_ACCOUNT_ID=your@email.com ECOVACS_PASSWORD=your_password scripts/data/update-eco-data.sh

On the first login from a new device, Ecovacs answers with error 1013 and the script triggers a device verification: a code is emailed to the account address and you are prompted for it.

Note

Verification codes are single-use and repeated requests are rate-limited by Ecovacs (0002 "Parameter error. Please try again later."). Wait 10-30 minutes before retrying. Verification is bound to the device id stored in .eco-device-id (gitignored), so subsequent runs log in directly without a code.

Step 2 - Refresh the codepush data (no login needed):

scripts/data/1-update-eco-codepush.sh
scripts/data/2-update-eco-codepush-mapping.sh

Step 3 - Download the CodePush packages (no login needed):

scripts/data/3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh

Only needed when the packages are to be served from Bumper (CODEPUSH_LOCAL_PACKAGE=true). The script downloads the package of every deployment of updateCheck.json, at the same time. The packages are large, so the deployments to fetch can be named:

CODEPUSH_DEPLOYMENT_KEYS=<the deployment key> scripts/data/3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh

The files are written to ${BUMPER_DATA}/codepush unless BUMPER_CODEPUSH says otherwise. For container/Swarm placement and the runtime switches, see Features: App Updates and Docker: Extra data files.

Step 4 - Refresh the time zones (needs an Ecovacs account):

ECOVACS_ACCOUNT_ID=your@email.com ECOVACS_PASSWORD=your_password scripts/data/update-eco-timezones.sh

The time zones are the same for every user, but the api wants a login. The host of the api belongs to the region of the account, API_BASE_HOST sets it.

Step 5 - Refresh the voice files (needs an Ecovacs account):

ECOVACS_ACCOUNT_ID=your@email.com ECOVACS_PASSWORD=your_password scripts/data/update-eco-voices.sh

Only needed when the robot is to change its voice language. The account login and the verification code work as in Step 1.

The files are written to ${BUMPER_DATA}/voices unless BUMPER_VOICES says otherwise, and the metadata to bumper/web/static_api/voices.json. For container/Swarm placement and voice behavior, see Features: Voice Languages and Docker: Extra data files.

items.title: 🔀 Combination Rules
items.text:
update-eco-data.sh combines the per-country responses with the currently committed files:

  • Country priority: each entry (by id / groupId / classid) is taken from DE if present, otherwise US, otherwise any other country; entries that no country supplies anymore are kept from the committed file.
  • Consistency: object keys are sorted recursively, so key reordering in upstream responses does not produce noisy diffs between runs.
  • Robustness: countries whose request failed are skipped instead of poisoning the combination.

items.title: ⚙️ Environment Variables
items.text: Variable Used by Purpose ECOVACS_ACCOUNT_ID, ECOVACS_PASSWORD update-eco-data.sh, update-eco-voices.sh Ecovacs account credentials (required) ECO_DEVICE_ID update-eco-data.sh, update-eco-voices.sh Stable device id (default: generated once and stored in .eco-device-id) ECO_DEVICE_ID_FILE update-eco-data.sh, update-eco-voices.sh Custom path for the device id file ECO_VERIFY_CODE update-eco-data.sh, update-eco-voices.sh Skip the prompt with a pre-fetched email verification code ECO_CHANNEL update-eco-data.sh App channel (google_play default; google worked in some regions) ECO_PARALLEL 1-update-eco-codepush.sh, 2-update-eco-codepush-mapping.sh, 3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh Number of parallel downloads (default 4) CODEPUSH_DEPLOYMENT_KEYS 3-update-eco-codepush-packages.sh Limit the download to the named deployment keys (comma separated) BUMPER_VOICES update-eco-voices.sh Where the voice files are written (default: ${BUMPER_DATA}/voices) VOICE_LANGS update-eco-voices.sh The languages to fetch, comma separated (default: every language) API_BASE_HOST update-eco-timezones.sh The api host of the region (default: api-base.dc-eu.ww.ecouser.net)

items.title: Web API Endpoints
items.text: This guide explains how a web route chooses its response shape, how @bind applies that shape, and which response template to start with when adding an endpoint. The route must preserve the exact JSON keys, value types, and failure shape expected by its client.

items.title: 🧭 The pieces
items.text:
Piece Job web.RouteTableDef Registers paths and HTTP methods in one plugin module. Route handler Reads the request, performs the operation, and returns the payload. Template Describes the success envelope and its corresponding ErrorShape. @bind(template) Converts a handler's payload or ApiError into the endpoint's response shape. TypedDict payload Names the fields and Python value types inside a response payload. Operation and dispatch Selects a handler and template when one URL has several operations.

The template describes the JSON envelope. It does not validate the payload's runtime type. Use type annotations and the payload definitions in bumper/web/payloads.py to make the payload shape clear to mypy and tests.

items.title: 🛣️ Register a route
items.text:
Every plugin module owns a web.RouteTableDef named routes. The package defines its prefix once in its __init__.py; modules use that prefix when registering paths. The web plugin loader discovers plugin modules, so a new module under bumper/web/plugins/ does not need a second route-registration edit.

from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp.web_request import Request

from bumper.web.envelope import GL_V1, bind

from . import BASE_URL

routes = web.RouteTableDef()


@routes.view(f"{BASE_URL}user/getBackupEmailByAccount")
@bind(GL_V1)
async def _handle_get_backup_email_by_account(request: Request) -> dict[str, str | None]:
    """Return the backup email fields expected by this endpoint."""
    return {"backUpEmail": None, "displayEmail": None}

Decorators are applied from the bottom up: bind wraps the handler first, then routes.view registers the wrapped handler. routes.view accepts any HTTP method. Prefer routes.get, routes.post, and the other method-specific registrations when the endpoint has a fixed method. Paths are case-sensitive.

A bound handler returns only the payload. It does not add code, ret, message, data, or other envelope fields itself. The binder owns those fields, including the error response shape.

items.title: 📦 What @bind does
items.text:
bind is implemented in bumper/web/envelope/binder.py:

  1. It calls the handler with the Request.
  2. If the handler returns a StreamResponse such as web.Response, it passes that response through unchanged. This is for files, images, and other raw documents.
  3. Otherwise, it passes the returned payload to Template.render and returns the rendered JSON.
  4. An ApiError is rendered using the template's ErrorShape, not its success shape. An uncaught exception is logged and returned with that error shape and HTTP status 500. web.HTTPException is re-raised.

For example, a handler bound to GL_V1 can return {"items": []}. The client receives the payload inside data, plus the GL_V1 success fields. If the handler raises ApiError(msg="No account", code=ERR_TOKEN_INVALID), the same route returns the GL_V1 error envelope. The handler does not need to choose either envelope itself.

Returning web.json_response(...) from a bound handler is usually wrong: it bypasses the template and its error handling. Return a payload instead. Return a Response only when the endpoint really is a raw response.

items.title: 🧱 Template fields
items.text:
Template is defined in bumper/web/envelope/templates.py. Its settings control the outer shape:

Setting Effect code, code_key Adds a status value under a key such as code. Use code=None when there is no status field or the key carries payload data. data_key Places the handler's payload under this key. None makes the payload flat. data_optional Omits the payload key when the handler returns None. Otherwise, None is serialized as JSON null. flat Merges a mapping payload into the response body instead of nesting it. result Adds a fixed result pair such as ("ret", "ok"). msg Adds a fixed message pair such as ("message", "success"). success Adds the boolean success field when set. time, time_value Adds the current time in milliseconds, or a fixed time value. todo Adds "todo": "result". extra Adds fixed side-car fields alongside the payload. error Selects the separate error envelope for the template.

ErrorShape controls failure keys such as errno, error, ret, todo, success, and time. A success template and its error shape need not have the same keys. Check both before using a template.

items.title: 🧾 Choose the response shape
items.text:
Start from the response contract of the endpoint or operation being added. Choose the template by the JSON shape, not by which template name seems cleanest.

Client-visible response Use Common location code: "0000", msg, data, success, and millisecond time GL_V1 Modern private API routes and global auth routes. code: 0, message, ret: "ok", and data LEGACY Standard /api/... JSON endpoints. Legacy envelope without a success ret field LEGACY_NO_RET or another matching LEGACY variant Endpoints whose success response omits ret. Legacy envelope with a flat payload and todo: "result" LEGACY_FLAT /api/users/user.do operations. Legacy envelope with todo: "result", ret: "ok", and data TODO_RET Older dispatcher endpoints such as app.do. {"todo":"result","result":"ok","code":...} where code is payload AUTH The newauth.do auth-code exchange. {"ret":"ok"} with no payload RET_ONLY Operations that answer only with a result flag. A file, image, or document body No template, or a bound handler returning Response Photo downloads and document endpoints. HTTP 200, empty body, outcome in x-ngiot-* headers response_ngiot_* helpers /api/iot/endpoint/control. This is not a JSON envelope.

LEGACY_BARE, LEGACY_MSG, and LEGACY_SUCCESS cover other legacy variants. Read their definitions and error shapes in templates.py rather than deriving one from a similar-looking template.

items.title: Typed payloads
items.text:
The payload type is separate from the envelope template. Define or reuse a TypedDict in bumper/web/payloads.py when a payload has named fields:

from typing import TypedDict


class ExampleInfo(TypedDict):
    """The information returned by the example endpoint."""

    id: str
    enabled: bool


@routes.get(f"{PREFIX}/example/info")
@bind(LEGACY)
async def _handle_example_info(_: Request) -> ExampleInfo:
    """Return the example payload, not the legacy envelope."""
    return {"id": "example", "enabled": True}

Use NotRequired[...] for keys that are genuinely optional in the payload. Do not make a field optional just because a value is unavailable in one test; the response shape is part of the client contract. Template.render accepts Any and does not enforce TypedDict at runtime, so keep the annotations, builder, and tests aligned.

items.title: 🔀 One path, several operations
items.text:
Some endpoints select their behavior by todo or td in the request body. Each operation can have a different response shape, so define an Operation table and dispatch through it. Do not bind one envelope around the whole path.

from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

from aiohttp import web
from aiohttp.web_request import Request
from bumper.web.envelope import LEGACY_FLAT
from bumper.web.operations import Operation, dispatch

from . import PREFIX

routes = web.RouteTableDef()
USER_DO_OPERATIONS: dict[str, Operation] = {}
routes.post(f"{PREFIX}/users/user.do")(dispatch(USER_DO_OPERATIONS, LEGACY_FLAT))


async def _handle_get_device_list(request: Request, post_body: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return the payload for this user.do operation."""
    return {"devices": []}


USER_DO_OPERATIONS.update(
    {"GetDeviceList": Operation(LEGACY_FLAT, _handle_get_device_list)},
)

The dispatcher reads the configured discriminator, invokes the operation handler, and renders its payload with that operation's template. The dispatcher template is the failure shape for an unknown operation. Operation handlers return payloads, not envelopes.

items.title: ⚡ Quick checklist
items.text:
Before implementing a route, answer these questions:

  1. Is it a JSON envelope, a raw file/document response, or the NGIoT header protocol?
  2. What exact success keys and value types does the client expect?
  3. What exact failure shape does this endpoint use? Can the handler raise ApiError and let the binder shape it?
  4. Does one path have multiple todo/td operations? If so, choose a template per operation with dispatch.
  5. Does the payload have a reusable typed shape? Put that TypedDict or its builder in bumper/web/payloads.py.
  6. Does the route path use the package prefix and the observed path casing?

If the answer shape is not known, do not invent a new template. Find an existing matching operation or gather the missing response contract first.

items.title: 🧪 Keep the response contract checked
items.text:
• Put each route in the plugin module that owns the API path. Keep the route declaration near the handler or operation table.
  • Add handler and payload tests under tests/web/, mirroring the source path.
  • scripts/api/api-table.py shows each route's bound response shape.
  • tests/web/routes.txt and tests/web/shapes.txt pin route registration and template selection. The pre-commit hook updates them when web routes change.
  • tests/web/response_shapes.json and tests/web/response_shapes_bumper.json check response keys and Python value types. A new key or changed type needs a reason in the response contract.
  • Run uv run --active --frozen pytest tests/web, the linters, and uv run --active --frozen zensical build --clean before contributing.

The core definitions are in bumper/web/envelope/templates.py, bumper/web/envelope/binder.py, and bumper/web/operations.py.

items.title: 🚀 Getting Started
items.text:
This guide walks through a complete Bumper setup: DNS, certificates, deployment, and connecting the app and robots. Bumper only works when every part of the path points at it - DNS, TLS trust, and the Bumper services.

Note

Bumper does not replace the Ecovacs cloud for every feature. It reimplements the parts needed for local control. Some cloud-only features are not available.

items.title: 📋 Before you start
items.text:
You need:

  • A server on your local network that can run Bumper (Docker is the recommended deployment).
  • A DNS server you control (Pi-hole, OPNsense/Unbound, dnsmasq, router DNS, etc.) that can override Ecovacs domains to your Bumper server.
  • A robot and/or client that can reach Bumper:
    • a robot already configured on your network, once its traffic is redirected to Bumper and it trusts Bumper's certificate; or
    • the official Ecovacs/Ecovacs Home app, configured to trust Bumper's CA and use your DNS; or
    • DeebotUniverse/client.py.

Check Model Compatibility for known reports and limitations. A missing model has not been reported; it may still work, but protocol and certificate behavior are model-dependent.

items.title: ✅ Setup checklist
items.text:
Follow these steps in order:

  1. DNS Setup - override Ecovacs domains so the app and robot resolve them to your Bumper server.
  2. Certificates - create TLS certificates before you use the checked-in Compose/Swarm files, which load $PWD/certs read-only: bash scripts/certs/create-cert.sh (add --rsa if your robot needs RSA).
  3. Deploy Bumper - run Bumper with Docker/Compose (recommended, usually behind nginx or Traefik). Set BUMPER_ANNOUNCE_IP to the server's LAN IP.
  4. Connect the Official App - install Bumper's CA on the phone and log in to the app.
  5. Robot Wi-Fi Setup - only if you need the app's Wi-Fi onboarding flow through Bumper. The server-side flow is handled by Bumper; the phone still configures the robot over the robot's setup access point.

items.title: The web UI
items.text:
Bumper's web UI (for example https://ecovacs.net/ when DNS points that name to Bumper) is a status and debug view. It shows information about connected clients and bots. It is not the place where you manually "add" a vacuum.

Seeing only helperbot is normal when no robot or app client is currently connected to Bumper.

items.title: When a robot appears
items.text:
A robot appears after it successfully connects to Bumper's MQTT/XMPP/web services and is identified by Bumper. That requires:

  • DNS/routing sends the robot's Ecovacs domains to Bumper.
  • Reachability through the ports and hostnames your deployment exposes. Bumper listens for HTTPS, HTTP, MQTT, MQTTS, and XMPP TLS; the defaults and their overrides are in Services and Environment Variables. In the recommended Docker + reverse proxy setup (nginx/Traefik), clients usually reach Bumper through the proxy. The proxy can route TLS on port 443 by SNI/hostname: for example, mq* hostnames to MQTTS and Ecovacs/Ecouser web hostnames to HTTPS, as configured in the provided nginx/Traefik examples. Some robots/apps may connect to native protocol ports directly when those ports are exposed. See Docker and the nginx/Traefik compose examples.
  • Certificate trust for the path the robot uses. Some models/apps need extra steps; see Model Compatibility and the certificate unpinning guides (APP, BOT).
  • Robot configuration: the robot must already be talking to those domains, or you must complete the onboarding flow.

If the app can reach Bumper but no robot appears, check Bumper logs, DNS resolution from the robot's network, certificate trust, and model-specific requirements.

items.title: The official app
items.text: The official app is optional for some setups (for example, command-line/control clients), but it is the usual way to verify connectivity and run onboarding flows. App behavior depends on app version, region, and model. Push notifications and other cloud-only features may not work.

items.title: 🛠️ Troubleshooting
items.text:
• ecovacs.net shows only helperbot / robot not appearing: work through the checklist under When a robot appears - DNS, reachability, certificate trust, and robot configuration, in that order. Confirm each step from the robot's network, not from the server.
  • Certificates missing or not trusted: the checked-in Compose/Swarm files load $PWD/certs/* read-only, so the files must exist before deployment. See Certificates for creating and installing them.
  • DNS not taking effect: test with dig/nslookup against the DNS server your device uses; clear caches or reboot the device/robot. See DNS Setup.
  • TLS/certificate errors: confirm the certificate matches the domains in use and that the client trusts the CA on the path it uses. App-side pinning and native TLS stacks may need Certificate Pinning Bypass (APP) or model-specific steps.
  • Need more detail: enable debug logging with Environment Variables and inspect container/server logs.

For user reports and questions, see Discussions.

items.title: 🔒 Certificates for Bumper
items.text: Bumper serves TLS for the app, robots, and its web UI. The certificates are self-signed: clients must trust Bumper's CA, and the server certificate must cover the Ecovacs hostnames clients connect to.

items.title: 📦 Files
items.text:
Both creation methods produce the same files:

File Created by Purpose ca.key scripts/certs/create-cert.sh or bumper/utils/certs.py Root CA private key ca.crt scripts/certs/create-cert.sh or bumper/utils/certs.py Root CA certificate - install/trust this on app and clients bumper.key scripts/certs/create-cert.sh or bumper/utils/certs.py Server private key bumper.crt scripts/certs/create-cert.sh or bumper/utils/certs.py Server certificate signed by the CA ca.pem scripts/certs/create-cert.sh or bumper/utils/certs.py Server key + server certificate + CA certificate (for mitmproxy)

Default key type is EC. Use RSA when a robot requires it: --rsa with the script, or CERT_KEY_TYPE=rsa with startup generation. The SAN list is defined by each implementation (scripts/certs/create-cert.sh and bumper/utils/certs.py).

items.title: 🧰 Option 1 - Create certificates with the host script
items.text:
The script uses OpenSSL on the host and writes files to $PWD/certs:

bash scripts/certs/create-cert.sh

# RSA instead of EC
bash scripts/certs/create-cert.sh --rsa

Behavior (idempotent):

  • if ca.crt or ca.key is missing, it creates a new CA and a new server certificate;
  • if the CA exists but bumper.crt or bumper.key is missing, it creates a new server certificate and keeps the existing CA (clients that already trust the CA keep working);
  • ca.pem is rebuilt if it is missing.

Use this when you want to create or rotate certificates yourself before starting Bumper.

items.title: 🐍 Option 2 - Let Bumper generate certificates at startup
items.text:
bumper.utils.certs.generate_certificates() runs during Bumper startup, before services listen. It writes the same five files to BUMPER_CERTS (default $PWD/certs / /bumper/certs in containers) when the directory is writable.

BUMPER_CERTS=$PWD/certs uv run --active bumper

Behavior:

  • if ca.crt, bumper.crt, and bumper.key all exist, generation is skipped (existing certificates are kept);
  • ca.key is not part of that existence check, so removing only ca.key does not trigger a new CA;
  • if only ca.pem is missing, it is rebuilt from the existing key and certificates;
  • changing CERT_KEY_TYPE later does not convert an existing certificate set.

Startup generation requires a writable certificates directory owned by (or writable for) the Bumper process (uid/gid 1000 in the container image). The checked-in Docker image starts as root, repairs ownership of /bumper/data and /bumper/certs when it can (CAP_CHOWN), then drops to bumper.

items.title: Generation settings
items.text:
Variable Default Effect BUMPER_CERTS ./certs Directory for generated files CERT_KEY_TYPE ec ec (ECDSA P-256) or rsa CERT_RSA_KEY_SIZE 2048 RSA key size when CERT_KEY_TYPE=rsa (2048-4096) BUMPER_CA_VALID_DAYS 6669 CA validity in days BUMPER_VALID_DAYS 666 Server certificate validity in days

Individual paths can be overridden with BUMPER_CA_CERT, BUMPER_CA_KEY, BUMPER_CA_PEM, BUMPER_CERT, and BUMPER_KEY.

items.title: 🐳 Checked-in Docker/Compose behavior
items.text:
The checked-in docker-compose.yaml and docker-compose-traefik.yaml load ca.crt, bumper.crt, and bumper.key as Docker configs from $PWD/certs/* and mount them read-only at /bumper/certs. The source files must exist before deployment:

bash scripts/certs/create-cert.sh
# add --rsa if your robot requires RSA keys

After creating them, install certs/ca.crt on devices/clients that need to trust Bumper.

Bumper's startup generation needs a writable /bumper/certs directory, so it does not run with these read-only config mounts. For a custom deployment where you want Bumper to generate certificates, mount a writable directory/volume at /bumper/certs instead of read-only config files. In Docker Swarm, host bind mounts are node-local; ensure the directory exists and is writable on the node that runs the task, or pre-create certificates with the host script (recommended for the checked-in Swarm files).

items.title: 📂 Custom certificates
items.text:
To use your own CA and server certificate, place files in the certificates directory before starting Bumper:

  • ca.crt, bumper.key, bumper.crt for Bumper
  • ca.pem for mitmproxy (optional)

The server certificate must include the Ecovacs hostnames and local addresses clients use. ca.pem contains the server private key; treat it as a secret and use it only for local tooling such as mitmproxy.

items.title: 🧪 mitmproxy
items.text:
Mount ca.pem into mitmproxy:

docker run --rm -it \
  -v $PWD/certs/ca.pem:/home/mitm/ca.pem:ro \
  mitmproxy/mitmproxy mitmweb \
    --certs '*=/home/mitm/ca.pem'

ca.pem is only needed by mitmproxy; Bumper uses the individual CRT/KEY files.

items.title: 🌐 DNS Configuration for Bumper
items.text: To intercept and redirect traffic from Ecovacs robots and the official app to your local Bumper server, configure your network's DNS resolver to override specific Ecovacs domains to your server's IP.

items.title: 🔧 Recommended: OPNsense + Unbound DNS
items.text:
If you're using OPNsense as your router/firewall, Unbound DNS is the default resolver. Override domain resolution by adding host overrides:

  1. Login to the OPNsense web interface.
  2. Navigate to Services → Unbound DNS → Overrides.
  3. Under Host Overrides, click Add and set:
    • Host: *
    • Domain: ecouser.net
    • IP: <BUMPER_SERVER_IP> (e.g. 192.168.1.100)
  4. Repeat for each of the other domains (host *, domain as below):
    • ecouser.com
    • ecovacs.com
    • ecovacs.net
  5. Click Apply to reload Unbound.

Note

These wildcard entries catch all subdomains under the specified domain.

items.title: 📦 Alternative: dnsmasq / Pi-hole
items.text:
If you're using DNSMasq directly or via Pi-hole, create a custom config file:

/etc/dnsmasq.d/02-bumper.conf

address=/ecouser.com/<BUMPER_SERVER_IP>
address=/ecouser.net/<BUMPER_SERVER_IP>
address=/ecovacs.com/<BUMPER_SERVER_IP>
address=/ecovacs.net/<BUMPER_SERVER_IP>

Replace <BUMPER_SERVER_IP> with your server's local IP (e.g. 192.168.1.100).

Apply changes:

  • dnsmasq: sudo systemctl reload dnsmasq
  • Pi-hole: pihole restartdns or via the web UI

items.title: ⚠️ Pi-hole v6 and dnsmasq.d
items.text:
Pi-hole v6 does not ingest custom configs in /etc/dnsmasq.d/ by default; this behavior is disabled in FTL. See Pi-hole discourse. You must explicitly re-enable it:

  • ENV: add FTLCONF_misc.dnsmasq_d=true
  • GUI: in the Pi-hole web UI, go to Settings > All settings page - Miscellaneous and enable the option.

Without this, custom 02-bumper.conf-style entries are silently ignored.

items.title: 📋 Notes on Domain Patterns
items.text:
If overriding DNS for top-level domains (like *.ecovacs.com) is not supported in your DNS setup, you must manually configure each relevant subdomain used by the app or robot.

EcoVacs robots and the companion app connect to different domains depending on country/region, app version, model, and firmware. Bumper does not care which exact domain is used, as long as the request reaches Bumper and is handled.

Note

The app may dynamically retrieve service/domain information from https://api-app.<region shard>.ecouser.net/api/appsvr/service/list (for example api-app.dc-eu.ww.ecouser.net). Required domains can vary across models, regions, and firmware versions.

items.title: Replacement Examples
items.text:
Most domains follow patterns based on country or region codes:

  • {country}: for gl-{country}-api.ecovacs.com and gl-{country}-openapi.ecovacs.com, use gl-de-api.ecovacs.com and gl-de-openapi.ecovacs.com for Germany. Country codes such as us, de, or jp appear here.
  • {region}: for portal-{region}.ecouser.net in North America, use portal-na.ecouser.net. {region} may also be eu, cn, or ww.

items.title: Summary
items.text:
• ✅ If your DNS supports wildcard or full-domain overrides, use them to catch all subdomains at once.
  • ❌ If it does not, manually define each used domain/subdomain.

items.title: 💡 Known Domains
items.text:
These are common domain patterns. The exact hostnames depend on app version, account region, and device model. Prefer wildcard DNS overrides when possible; if your resolver cannot use wildcards, monitor DNS traffic and add the specific hostnames your device requests.

Pattern Purpose lb*.ecouser.net Load-balancer discovery portal*.ecouser.net Login and REST API gl-{country}-api.ecovacs.com, gl-{country}-openapi.ecovacs.com Modern app API api-app*.ecouser.net, api-rop.dc-{region}.ww.ecouser.net, users-base.dc-{region}.ww.ecouser.net App v2+ REST APIs and accounts msg*.ecouser.net XMPP mq*.ecouser.net, jmq-ngiot-*.ecouser.net MQTT / NGIoT *.iot-as-mqtt.*.aliyuncs.com, *.itls.*.aliyuncs.com Aliyun IoT MQTT endpoints (observed with app/NGIoT traffic) kinesisvideo.{region}.amazonaws.com, *.kinesisvideo.{region}.amazonaws.com Observed in live-video/KVS experiments; not part of standard Bumper setup recommender.ecovacs.com, bigdata-*.ecovacs.com, sa-eu-datasink.ecovacs.com Optional telemetry/recommendation services

items.title: 🔒 Certificate and Trust Notes
items.text:
Bumper's certificate covers many intercepted host patterns, but SAN coverage alone does not make a host work: DNS must reach Bumper, the certificate must be valid for that name, and the client must trust the CA on the path it uses.

Two paths can still refuse a user-installed CA: the app's MQTT pin and channels with a native TLS stack (NGIoT, Aliyun IoT MQTT). See Certificates, App Certificate Unpinning, and The app on the wire.

items.title: 🔍 Troubleshooting
items.text:
• App won't connect: test overrides with dig or nslookup against your DNS server to confirm the Ecovacs domains resolve to your Bumper IP.
  • Partial redirects: clear the device DNS cache or reboot the robot and used device.
  • IPv6 issues: if your network uses IPv6, add corresponding AAAA records for each domain.
  • Pi-hole v6 ignores 02-bumper.conf: verify that FTLCONF_misc.dnsmasq_d=true (or the GUI equivalent) is enabled so FTL consumes /etc/dnsmasq.d/.

items.text:

  • Pi-hole documentation

items.title: 📶 Robot Wi-Fi Onboarding
items.text: Bumper answers the server side of the official app's Wi-Fi setup for MQTT robots. The phone still talks to the robot's setup access point; Bumper does not configure the robot's Wi-Fi. Bumper starts the setup, waits for the robot to connect, and then returns the robot identity to the app.

items.title: 🔄 Flow
items.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as Ecovacs app
    participant B as Bumper
    participant R as Robot access point
    participant M as Robot MQTT client

    App->>B: DecodeQrCode / getConfigGroups
    App->>B: PreWifiConfig (sck)
    B-->>App: {"ret":"ok"}
    App->>R: SetApConfig (SSID, password, broker data)
    R->>M: join the home Wi-Fi
    loop while setup is pending
        App->>B: PollSCResult (sck)
        B-->>App: pending, or the robot identity
    end
    M->>B: MQTT login
    M->>B: iot/scsync/<poll key>
    App->>B: GetGlobalDeviceList (did)

items.title: ✅ How Bumper completes a setup
items.text:
1. PreWifiConfig* opens one in-memory setup slot for the app user. The slot lives for 30 minutes.
  2. While the robot has not connected, PollSCResult answers the pending shape from the official server: ret: fail, errno: 600, subCode: 1. Bumper adds a short debug hint, which the app ignores.
  3. A robot authenticates to Bumper's MQTT broker and publishes iot/scsync/<key>. The setup completes when that key matches the poll key from the same app user's setup flow.
  4. The next poll answers with the robot identity: {"ret":"ok","did":…,"type":…,"resource":…,"name":…}.
  5. The MQTT login already created the bot record, so GetGlobalDeviceList returns the new bot. When the request carries a did, Bumper returns only that device, which is what the app asks for after setup.

The sck sent with PreWifiConfig and the sck sent with PollSCResult can differ. The app user is the stable link between the two calls, so Bumper does not require the keys to be equal.

After success the app may also call homed/device/move, device/blacklist/check, member/getBindBenefit, and users/user.do with todo: SetDeviceNick. Bumper answers those requests; device/move is a no-op because Bumper reports every device in its default home.

items.title: 🚫 What Bumper does not do
items.text:
• It does not implement the robot's local setup endpoint (http://192.168.0.1:8888/rcp.do, SetApConfig). The phone must reach the robot's access point and send the Wi-Fi credentials itself.
  • It does not create a DID, password, class, or resource for a factory-fresh robot. The robot must already have usable credentials.
  • It does not change the robot's certificate trust. Some firmware trusts an embedded Ecovacs CA and will not accept Bumper's generated certificate without a device-side change.
  • It supports one setup at a time. A second PreWifiConfig replaces the active slot.

items.title: 📋 Requirements for a working setup
items.text:
1. The app and the robot must reach Bumper's web and MQTT services.
  2. The robot must trust Bumper's TLS certificate and authenticate with credentials Bumper accepts.
  3. The robot's class must exist in Bumper's product map, so the device list can describe it.
  4. The phone must be able to complete the local AP handoff; Bumper cannot do that part.

items.title: 🔍 Verifying a setup
items.text:
A successful run looks like this in the Bumper log:

  1. PreWifiConfig returns ok.
  2. The first PollSCResult returns the pending shape.
  3. The robot authenticates over MQTT.
  4. The robot publishes iot/scsync/<poll key>.
  5. The next PollSCResult returns the robot identity.
  6. GetGlobalDeviceList with the new did returns one device, and the app opens that robot.

If the poll stays pending, check the robot's MQTT login, its iot/scsync publish, the app user on both setup calls, and whether the class is present in the product map. A phone-to-robot AP failure happens before Bumper is involved; Bumper cannot see or repair it.

items.title: How It Works
items.text:
Disclaimer

This document is a work in progress and may contain inaccuracies or incomplete sections. Some parts serve as placeholders and require further refinement. Please refer to the source code for authoritative information, and feel free to submit corrections or improvements.

Bumper recreates Ecovacs's cloud services locally, so supported robots and apps can work inside your network. The app uses the web API for discovery, accounts, and Wi-Fi onboarding. For live traffic it uses XMPP with older robots and MQTT with newer ones, and a robot speaks exactly one of the two. Robots authenticate and exchange onboarding messages over their live protocol. Supported robots also POST data to the web API over HTTPS.

The app and the robot reach Bumper over TLS. The app connects to mq*.ecouser.net on port 443, and to the web hosts on 443 as well, so the shipped nginx/Traefik listener reads the SNI: an mq* host goes to the MQTT broker, every other Ecovacs host goes to the web server. XMPP keeps its own port 5223. The app provisions a robot with the same 443 broker endpoint; Bumper also listens on 8883 for robots configured with that port.

items.title: 🔐 Account and Authentication
items.text:
Bumper recreates the account and token plumbing the app expects, but it does not verify Ecovacs request signatures. The app logs in with an account name, receives an opaque access token, exchanges an IoT token for an auth code, and then receives OAuth tokens. The same auth code links the account to the XMPP or MQTT transport.

The account key is separate from the TLS key. The private half stays in the data directory, so Bumper can read the fields the app encrypts and no other server can.

One account has several public names, and each app installation has its own client id and resource with its own token row, so parallel installations stay separate. See Authentication for the full flow, the trust model, the ids and alias rules, and the known gaps.

items.title: 🌐 Web Server and REST API
items.text:
Bumper's web server simulates the Ecovacs REST API for login and command routing:

  • Discovery: the app retrieves the service endpoints from Bumper over HTTPS. Every endpoint mirrors a service the app expects, and the hostname in the answer picks which Bumper service answers. Robots do not use this discovery; they use the server and broker they were provisioned with.
  • Robot HTTP uploads: the robot-originated HTTP path observed in Bumper is /data_collect/upload/generalData (or /api/idi/data_collect/upload/generalData). It accepts map/job documents and camera pictures; Bumper stores them for the app and web UI. This is separate from the app's HTTP requests for account, discovery, and Wi-Fi onboarding flows.
  • Authentication: the app submits account/login data expected by the Ecovacs flow. Bumper creates/finds local records as needed and returns compatible tokens/codes; the HTTP layer does not verify Ecovacs request signatures.
  • Command routing: when the app issues a command (for example, start cleaning), Bumper accepts the request and hands it to the MQTT helper bot, which publishes it to the robot. XMPP robots are controlled by stanzas the app sends through the XMPP server, not through the web API.
  • Status queries: the app can poll REST endpoints for state/telemetry that Bumper has stored or relayed.

These paths mirror the patterns the app expects, so the app works unmodified.

items.title: 🔗 XMPP Protocol
items.text:
Example Models: Ozmo 601, Ozmo 930

  1. Discovery
    • The REST service list (/api/appsvr/service/list) names the XMPP service as msg-eu.<domain>:5223.
    • DNS resolves that name to Bumper, which listens on 5223.
  2. Connection
    • Both robot and app open TLS on port 5223 to Bumper's XMPP Server.
  3. Message Relay
    • Bumper maintains separate sessions for each side and forwards XML stanzas.
    • Commands (e.g., start/stop) and status (e.g., battery) are exchanged as XMPP messages.
  4. Keep-Alive
    • Bumper responds to XMPP pings and sends heartbeats to prevent timeouts.

Tip

The XMPP listener is its own port. It is not part of the 443 SNI split, so the app and the robot dial msg-eu.<domain>:5223 directly.

items.title: ☁️ MQTT Protocol
items.text:
Example Models: Deebot 600, 900, 901, Ozmo 950

  1. Broker Connection
    • Robot connects to Bumper's MQTT Broker on 8883 (TLS), 1883 (plain), or 443 through the SNI listener, depending on the endpoint it was provisioned with.
    • The app connects to mq*.ecouser.net:443. The host is built into the app, not read from the REST service list, so the 443 listener must route it to the broker by SNI.
  2. Telemetry Publishing
    • Robot publishes JSON status to iot/atr/<event>/<did>/<class>/<resource>/<payload type>, for example on onStats and reportStats.
    • The broker forwards the message to every subscriber, so the app gets live status and Bumper records it.
  3. Command Delivery
    • App calls a REST endpoint such as /api/iot/endpoint/control.
    • Web Server hands the command to the Helper Bot.
    • Helper Bot publishes it to iot/p2p/<command>/<sender did>/<sender class>/<sender resource>/<receiver did>/<receiver class>/<receiver resource>/q/<request id>/<payload type>.
  4. Response Handling
    • Robot answers on an iot/p2p/... topic with p in the request/response position and the same request id.
    • Helper Bot matches the answer to the waiting request and returns it to the REST call.

items.title: ⚙️ Helper Bot
items.text:
• An internal MQTT client that bridges REST API calls to MQTT topics.
  • Connects to the broker's plain listener on 1883, with a fixed client id that the broker accepts before any other check.
  • Subscribes to the robot's iot/atr telemetry and to the iot/p2p replies addressed to it, so it can keep the bot record current and match an answer to the waiting REST call by message ID.

For further details, see the source modules in bumper/web/server.py, bumper/xmpp/xmpp.py, and bumper/mqtt/server.py.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
Bumper reproduces the account and token plumbing the Ecovacs app expects, but it does not reproduce the cloud's security model. The app must work on a LAN without an Ecovacs account, so Bumper accepts the identity the client names and issues its own tokens. This page describes both sides: what the official app does, and what Bumper does with it.

The important consequence is at the top: HTTP request signatures are not verified. JWTs are verified when Bumper uses their claims as proof of account ownership.

items.title: 🔐 Trust model
items.text:
Bumper is built for a trusted local network. It:

  • accepts an account name without checking a password,
  • issues an app token for any account name,
  • accepts the app's encrypted fields but does not verify who sent them,
  • decodes some bearer-token claims for request context without checking the signature,
  • lets the MQTT and XMPP servers skip token checks because USE_AUTH is False.

The TLS CA is the real trust boundary. A device that trusts Bumper's CA can talk to Bumper; Bumper does not establish a second identity for it. Do not expose the web, MQTT, or XMPP listeners to an untrusted network.

USE_AUTH in bumper/utils/settings.py is a code constant, not an environment variable. Setting it to True enables secret checks in MQTT and XMPP. The checks accept a live portal token, auth code, or IT token, or a valid access JWT signed by this Bumper instance. It does not make the HTTP API verify request signatures.

items.title: 🧩 Identity layers
items.text:
The account and each app installation have separate identities:

Identity Used by Shape / role Account id (A) app and modern API YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_<32 lowercase hex> Unified id (U) IoT auth-code exchange same shape as A, generated independently IoT id (I) OAuth and legacy transports 16 lowercase letters or digits Client id (K) OAuth and app-installation row 24 lowercase hex characters Resource (R) XMPP/MQTT connection and client client-provided resource string App device id (D) app path and device ownership generated by the app Robot id robot, MQTT, XMPP serial number or device id, depending on robot generation

Bumper stores the account in BumperUser (bumper/web/utils/models.py) and the short-lived session data in Token (bumper/db/tokens.py). The user record carries A, U, I, the login name, aliases, app device ids, and the robots known to the local service. Each local account receives the shared robot list. Each token row carries one portal token and its related IT token, auth code, K, R, and device id. ClientRepo stores the live connection state for each app client/resource.

items.title: How the user id is made
items.text:
New accounts receive independent A, U, and I values. A is also the internal userid of a newly created account. Existing records keep their internal id; when first used, Bumper adopts a presented public id into an empty field or generates a missing id, and retains the old id as an alias. The pre-redesign 20-character SHA-256-derived id is recognized as a legacy alias, not generated as the new public account id.

Login resolves the provided name case-insensitively. For login2, Bumper decrypts encryptAccount with its local account key and stores the result as the login name. The encrypted password is accepted but not checked. If no name is provided, the configured USER_USERNAME_DEFAULT is used.

items.title: One account, several names
items.text:
The app does not use one name for an account. It logs in with a login name, uses A and U during the modern flow, and uses I for OAuth and legacy transports. Each app installation also has a device id and client/resource pair. Bumper keeps one BumperUser per account and resolves its public ids and legacy ids as aliases (bumper/db/identity.py). Accounts with different login names remain separate unless a shared device, presented account id, or valid token links them.

When a name resolves to a second user record and the link is proven - the token names one record and the request names the other, or the app device is bound to one record and the request names the other - the older record wins. The duplicate's devices, robots, homes, tokens, and clients move to the older record, and its id becomes an alias. Startup also merges duplicate public ids, login names, and app-device ownership before reconciling client rows. Rows with no account owner are removed; rows carrying an account alias are moved to the canonical account. Distinct client ids or resources remain distinct rows.

checkLogin never creates a user. It resolves an unknown name by the app device and fails if neither is known, because a check is not a registration. The normal login creates an account when the login name is new, then binds the device to it. Reusing the same login name resolves to the same account.
